newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler says fuel cell car ahead of schedule.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says fuel cell car ahead of schedule.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG is running well ahead of schedule in developing a so-called "fuel cell" car which produces almost no exhaust and does not rely on batteries for power, Chairman Juergen Schrempp said on Wednesday.

Speaking at the company's annual shareholder meeting, Schrempp said, "within a short time we have made a quantum jump and in two-years the first all-wheel drive fuel-cell car in the world will be ready to roll."
Unlike electric cars that rely on batteries, the Daimler fuel cell cars would produce their own energy on board by converting methanol into hydrogen which is then mixed with oxygen to produce energy.
The process produces very little exhaust other than a small amount of water and none of the noise that internal combustion engines make.
In the past Daimler, has fitted out prototype vans with the technology, but now says it is ready to equip an ordinary car.
Schrempp said Daimler will show one of its new A-Class cars with a fuel-cell power plant in October at the Tokyo Motor Show.
